newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - April 9.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - April 9.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
** Corporate India braces for the worst as countrywide truck strick continues -- automobile makers begin to cut production, the Economic Times newspaper reports
** Ruling United Front coalition says it will begin formal talks with the Congress party, raising hopes of a solution to the country's 10-day-old political crisis
** The United Front says the fate of the country's 1997/98 federal budget depends on the survival of the government
** Stock markets nervously await crucial confidence vote that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda faces on April 11
** Reserve Bank of India will seek a balance between loosening credit while keeping monetary growth in check when it presents a half-yearly strategy paper next week
The central bank unveils its monetary and credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) on April 15
** Farmers in agriculturally-rich northern Indian states clash with the government over wheat purchase prices threatening procurement operations amid falling stocks, trade and state officials says
** Software firm Infosys Technologies offers bonus equity shares in the proportion of one share for every share held
Infosys says its 1996/97 (April-March) net climbs to 369.8 million rupees, from 210.1 million a year earlier
The company says it recommends an increase in the holdings of foreign institutional investors to 30 percent from the current 24
** Stock markets in Bombay stay closed on Tuesday for a local festival, but shares on other regional bourses rise after Congress says it is ready for talks with crippled government
Bombay's benchmark stocks index closes 29.88 points, or 0.84 percent, to 3429.26 on Monday
** Indian rupee opens Wednesday rock steady at 35.86/87 against the dollar
